title: Ways To Boost Home Comfort with a Zoning System
desc: Read our blog to learn ways you can boost home comfort with a zoning system. Call Rosenberg Indoor Comfort today!

blocks.text: In a conventional forced-air system, one thermostat controls the temperature for the entire house. But sometimes you only need to use one or two rooms. In those instances, a conventional system will still run and consume the same amount of energy. In this article, we’ll look at how zoning can help save you money and boost your San Antonio home’s comfort.
1. Enhance Temperature Control

A zoning system will have multiple air handlers that allow you to control airflow for separate rooms. Every contiguous area has a thermostat that records temperatures that will tell the air handler when to start. That means you don’t have to condition those areas of your home you don’t use frequently.

Conventional heating systems will heat all parts of the building simultaneously. Even when you are only using one room, your furnace will keep running. As a result, they end up wasting a lot of energy, which will keep raising your utility bills.
2. Effective Approach to Adding an Extra Room

Another benefit of zoning is that some areas of your home may have unique heating and cooling needs. Perhaps some rooms have features such as high ceilings, lofts, or large windows. Such features may create variations in terms of their heating or cooling demands.
Also, some parts may receive more direct sunlight, and therefore, may be warmer than the rest of the house. To tackle these challenges, you could opt for a ductless mini-split system.

A ductless mini-split system has up to four indoor units and a conduit connecting to the outdoor unit. You can place the air handler in different areas of your home to create heating zones. Their small footprint makes it easy to set up.

The installation of a mini-split system is less expensive compared to the installation of a traditional forced-air system. It is often the best solution when you need to extend heating to an extra room in your home as it may be impractical to extend the ductwork from your existing system.
3. Boost Comfort and Convenience

Zoning is the most efficient solution if you’ve ever wanted to have varying temperatures for different rooms. The respective indoor units will raise or lower the temperatures when necessary. So you can tailor each zone so that it conditions only the areas that are occupied.
With programmable thermostats, you can customize temperature regulation more precisely. The most recent versions allow you to access their settings from your computer or a portable device.
Combined with zoning, smart devices can conveniently boost comfort in your San Antonio Home. For example, you can set your system to warm up the living room just before you get home from work.

A ductless system usually has a smaller footprint and fewer components. It runs less frequently and more quietly than conventional HVAC systems. That means more comfort when you need to extend your heating system to a cozy guest room or mother-in-law suite.
4. Improve Your Indoor Air Quality

In zoning systems, the airflow to different zones is controlled independently by each of the air handlers. You can adjust the airflow in each zone and set it just how you want it. That means that there is a lower chance that pollutants in one of the rooms will spread throughout your home.

Additionally, the ductwork in conventional systems can harbor dust, debris, and pollen. You need to schedule maintenance more frequently to reduce the threat of pollutants getting into your home. On the other hand, zoned systems are less likely to pose an indoor air quality problem.
5. Make Your Equipment Last Longer

Another cost-saving benefit of zoning is that zoning systems have fewer parts and therefore require less maintenance. They last longer since, unlike conventional systems, they do not have to overwork to regulate temperatures in your home.

They also don’t need your typical ductwork set up, which means that they are less expensive to install. You can also avoid issues related to leaky ductwork, such as spores, microbes, and a spike in utility bills. Traditional systems are prone to contamination, which is not only a hazard but can also damage your equipment.
